gloss: past and present; then and now

definitions.gloss: past and present; then and now
definitions.explanation: The contrast or comparison between how things were in the past and how they are now. Often used to reflect on changes over time.

examples.japanese: {今昔|こんじゃく}の{感|かん}がある。
examples.english: I feel a sense of how things have changed.

examples.japanese: この{写真|しゃしん}を{見|み}ると{今昔|こんじゃく}の{感|かん}に{堪|た}えない。
examples.english: Looking at this photo, I can't help but feel how much things have changed.

examples.japanese: {東京|とうきょう}の{今昔|こんじゃく}を{写真|しゃしん}で{比較|ひかく}する{展示|てんじ}が{人気|にんき}を{集|あつ}めている。
examples.english: An exhibition comparing photos of Tokyo then and now is drawing crowds.

notes:
A literary compound expressing the contrast between past and present. Most commonly encountered in the set phrase {今昔|こんじゃく}の{感|かん} (a feeling of how times have changed) and in the title of the famous literary work {今昔|こんじゃく}{物語集|ものがたりしゅう}.

FORMATION:
{今|こん} (now, present) + {昔|じゃく} (past, old times). Note the on'yomi reading じゃく for {昔|じゃく}, which differs from the common kun'yomi むかし.

KEY EXPRESSIONS:
- {今昔|こんじゃく}の{感|かん}: a feeling of how times have changed — the most common usage
- {今昔|こんじゃく}の{感|かん}に{堪|た}えない: to be overwhelmed by the sense of change
- {今昔|こんじゃく}{物語集|ものがたりしゅう}: Konjaku Monogatari (a Heian-period collection of tales from Japan, China, and India)

RELATED TERMS:
- {昔|むかし}: the past, old times — everyday word
- {往時|おうじ}: the past, former days — literary
- {隔世|かくせい}の{感|かん}: a sense of being in a different era — similar nuance to {今昔|こんじゃく}の{感|かん}
